key_insight: A wall-shear neural estimator can be highly accurate offline yet still destabilize opposition control in closed loop because control-induced distribution shift breaks dynamic consistency.
engineering_relevance: For wall-only flow control, deployment must be designed for closed-loop robustness, not just reconstruction accuracy, if drag reduction is to persist in real operation.
method: Train a recurrent estimator to infer near-wall detection-plane velocity from the two wall-shear-stress components.
Test the estimator both offline and inside the opposition-control feedback loop.
Restore stability with spectral consistency in the actuation and retraining on closed-loop data.
evidence_signal: Offline, the estimator reached correlation 0.99 with near-unity coherence, but in closed loop it decorrelated within a few viscous time units as control collapsed.
watch_item: Low-pass filtering and exponential averaging can delay failure, but they do not solve the underlying distribution-shift and may still allow instability.
paper_title: Offline accuracy is not enough: closed-loop instability and stabilisation of a wall-sensor neural estimator in opposition control
